findings.claim: The catch block now builds its error message with getRtkQueryErrorMessage(e) instead of a fixed string, but no test exists for IdentitySection or its parent GeneralPage, and the only coverage nearby exercises a separate copy of this logic in useUpdateSpace.ts used by UpdateSpaceDialog. As a result this line could be reverted to the old fixed-string behavior and the full test suite would still pass, leaving the main workspace-rename page covered only by a Cypress happy-path test.
No test exists that rejects unwrap() with a {status: 422, data: {message}} shape and checks the message is shown, nor one covering the {status: 500, data: {}} fallback case.
The value caught in catch (e) is unknown but is force-cast to FetchBaseQueryError | SerializedError with `as`, without any runtime check that it actually matches either shape.

If a plain JS Error is thrown inside the try block, the cast in the catch sends it down the SerializedError branch and the raw error.message (e.g. a property-access error) is shown to the user, which is exactly what this helper's doc comment says must never happen; before this change users saw fixed friendly copy instead.

If a primitive value (a string or undefined) is thrown instead of an object, the `'status' in error` check inside the helper throws a TypeError from within the catch block, so no error message is shown to the user and the resulting promise rejection goes unhandled.
The same unchecked cast of a caught unknown error to FetchBaseQueryError | SerializedError already exists here, outside this diff, so the same failure mode applies.

The helper that formats RTK error messages has no guard for values that are not RTK error shapes; it should accept unknown and fall back to RTK_QUERY_ERROR_MESSAGES.generic for anything that isn't a recognizable FetchBaseQueryError or SerializedError, and callers should use that guard instead of casting with `as`.

The new error-path tests only check that the error text appears; they never assert that the success actions (trackEvent, the success notification, handleClose/onClose) were not called, so deleting the early return that guards them would not be caught by any test.

Only an early return at this line prevents the success actions from running after a failed operation, and this behavior is untested, so a failed role change could show a success message and close the dialog without any test failing.
EditMemberDialog has no success-path test at all, and the thrown-exception branch (as opposed to a rejected unwrap) is not tested.
